newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE mission to leave for Albania on Friday.
newsitem.headline: OSCE mission to leave for Albania on Friday.

text.p: An OSCE special mission to Albania headed by former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, will travel to the troubled Balkan state via Italy on Friday, instead of Thursday as planned, an OSCE spokeswoman said.

"We are leaving early tomorrow morning for Bari in Italy, from where we will be helicoptered to an Italian ship off the Albanian coast around mid-morning," the spokeswoman for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) told Reuters.

It was unclear whether the 10-member mission would travel to Tirana or meet government and rebel representatives on the ship, in an effort to resolve the worsening crisis in Albania, sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.

"We are not sure yet where we will meet representatives of the government and the rebels. In any case...we will try to go on land and reach Tirana or try to have them reach us on the ship," the spokeswoman said.
She added that it had been impossible to land at the airport in Tirana, which was closed after a nearby military base was looted.
The delegation was due to leave Vienna in an Italian military plane at 6 a.m. (0500 GMT) on Friday, she said, noting the visit was expected to last one day.
A spokeswoman at Vienna airport confirmed that an Italian military plane was expected to arrive there later on Thursday.

Vranitzky, who first visited Tirana last week on behalf of the OSCE, told a news conference earlier he would do all he could to reach Albania in the hope of holding the talks, as the country plunged deeper into a state of anarchy.

"The next important step is to involve the rebels in the political process," said Vranitzky, who earlier presented his report on the current conflict in Albania to the OSCE's Vienna-based permanent council.

"We have had no direct reaction (regarding dialogue) from anyone on behalf of the insurgents, but the message from the prime minister (Bashkim Fino) is that we may be able to have contact and might be able to organise talks," Vranitzky said.

He said the OSCE at this stage saw no need for NATO intervention but hours after he made his comments, Albania's interim government called on NATO's European members to provide military assistance to restore order in the Balkan country.
The former chancellor stressed that cooperation between political and financial institutions in Europe was vital to help resolve the crisis, since the OSCE could not do the job single-handedly.

"The World Bank and International Monetary Fund are immediately prepared to talk to Albania, on two conditions: the restoration of public order and the clear commitment to democratic politics in Albania," he said.
